# #010. Boss: Reduced Costs & New-Product Break-Even

<!-- section:scenario -->
Welcome to the **Chapter 1 Boss**! Your plant currently manufactures $B$ existing products (`baseMargins`) sharing $M$ factory resources (`capacities`). R&D proposes $C$ new **candidate products** (`candidateMargins`) that consume the same resources: the full consumption matrix `usages` has $M$ rows and $B + C$ columns (first the $B$ base products, then the $C$ candidates).

Management asks three unified questions:
1. If all $B + C$ products compete together in one joint LP, what are the optimal production levels (`baseQuantities`, `candidateQuantities`) and maximum `optimalProfit`?
2. What are the resource `shadowPrices` $y_k \ge 0$ at that joint optimum?
3. For each candidate $c$, what is its **reduced cost** $r_c = \text{candidateMargins}[c] - \sum_k \text{usages}[k][B + c] \, y_k \le 0$ (`v.reducedCost` / `col_dual`), and how much must its unit margin increase (`minMarginIncreaseNeeded[c] = max(0, -r_c)`) before it breaks even against existing products?

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P010Input`)**:
  - `baseMargins: number[]` (length $B$), `candidateMargins: number[]` (length $C$)
  - `usages: number[][]` — $M \times (B + C)$ consumption matrix
  - `capacities: number[]` — length $M$ resource limits
- **Output (`P010Output`)**:
  - `baseQuantities: number[]`, `candidateQuantities: number[]` — optimal continuous quantities
  - `optimalProfit: number` — joint maximum profit
  - `shadowPrices: number[]` — shadow prices $y_k$ of the joint LP
  - `candidateReducedCosts: number[]` — reduced cost $r_c \le 0$ for each candidate
  - `minMarginIncreaseNeeded: number[]` — `max(0, -candidateReducedCosts[c])`

<!-- section:example -->
- **Case 1**: Base `[50, 40]` already earn `2,800` with shadow prices `[20, 10, 0]`. Candidate 0 earns `20` per unit while consuming `2*20 + 3*10 = 70` worth of bottleneck capacity (`reducedCost = -50`), so it sits at `0` unless R&D lifts its margin by at least **`+50`**.
- **Case 2**: Candidate 0 earns `75` and actually **beats** the opportunity cost of existing products! In the joint optimum, `candidateQuantities[0] > 0`, `candidateReducedCosts[0] = 0`, and `minMarginIncreaseNeeded[0] = 0`!

<!-- section:hint1 -->
Do **not** optimize only over the $B$ base products and evaluate candidates separately — in Case 2 Candidate 0 shifts the active bottleneck basis! Build a single joint LP with $B + C$ non-negative variables `allVars` against `usages` and `capacities`.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
After `await m.solve()` (or `sol = h.getSolution()` in `highspy`), every non-negative variable already exposes its exact LP reduced cost!
- **WaSHI**: **`v.reducedCost`** (note `Math.abs(rc) < 1e-9 ? 0 : rc`), or compute directly `candMargin - sum_k usages[k][B+c] * shadowPrices[k]`.
- **highspy**: **`sol.col_dual[v.index]`** equals $c_j - A_{\cdot j}^\top y \le 0$ in maximization! Then **`minMarginIncreaseNeeded[c] = Math.max(0, -rc)`**.

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\max_{x \ge 0} \quad & c_{\text{base}}^\top x_{\text{base}} + c_{\text{cand}}^\top x_{\text{cand}} \quad \text{s.t.} \; A x \le b \\
r_c &= c_{\text{cand}, c} - \sum_{k=0}^{M-1} a_{k, B+c} \, y_k^* \le 0 \\
\Delta_{\text{break-even}, c} &= \max(0, -r_c)
\end{aligned}
$$

**Pricing out** new activities using dual shadow prices ($r_j = c_j - A_{\cdot j}^\top y^*$) is the exact engine behind the Simplex pivot rule and **Column Generation** — which you will use later in Chapter 8!
